ModifyVulnerableMultiplier.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and N2 per binding rule 4. NOT a Hook override: PaperPhrog.cs:16 is a plain public method, and its ONE caller is VulnerablePower.ModifyDamageMultiplicative, which looks the relic up directly on the dealer (`dealer.Player?.GetRelic<PaperPhrog>()`, VulnerablePower.cs:40-44). The sim turns that direct lookup into a real hook chain, which is where G1's divergence in the DISPATCH SET comes from; the +0.25 itself (PaperPhrog.cs:26 vs paper_phrog.py:23) and the 1.5 base it modifies (VulnerablePower.cs:22's `DamageIncrease` 1.5m vs powers.py:411) match, with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in either file.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): C# consults the dealer's phrog ONCE by direct lookup; the sim runs a hook chain over every combat listener, so N copies of the relic would each add 0.25
guards.issue: MECHANISM: VulnerablePower.cs:40-44 does `dealer.Player?.GetRelic<PaperPhrog>()` and calls the method on that single instance, so the bonus is applied at most once no matter what. hooks.py:190-193 folds `mult` through EVERY listener that defines modify_vulnerable_multiplier, so two instances of the relic in run.relics would give +0.50. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the concrete unported thing is named): the sim's only duplicate-relic mechanism is Toy Box's wax copies (Relic.is_wax, relics/base.py:102-104), and a wax Paper Phrog in the same run as the real one would double the bonus. Whether Toy Box can produce a wax copy of an already-held relic is a question about relic/toy_box, which is not audited on this branch, so this is filed dormant rather than live -- porting or confirming any path that puts two Paper Phrogs in one run makes it live. Ordering is NOT part of this divergence: C# applies phrog, then CrueltyPower, then DebilitatePower (VulnerablePower.cs:43-55) and the sim applies cruelty inline before the hook (powers.py:413-417), but every contribution is additive so the sum is order-independent; DebilitatePower has no sim counterpart and is a separate unit's concern.

guards.what: N1: `if (!props.IsPoweredAttack()) return amount;` (PaperPhrog.cs:22-25) -- the sim's port has no props parameter at all
guards.rationale: STRUCTURALLY SATISFIED, and doubly so. C#'s own caller already returned 1m for non-powered damage two lines earlier (VulnerablePower.cs:33-36), so the relic's copy of the check is dead weight in the source too. On the sim side the gate is enforced one level higher: DamageCmd.deal only calls modify_damage_multiplicative at all when `is_powered_attack(props)` (cmds.py:56-58, valueprops.py:47-49 = Move AND NOT Unpowered, matching ValuePropExtensions.cs:5-12), so unpowered damage never reaches VulnerablePower's multiplier, let alone the relic's hook. Checked by reading the props plumbing end to end rather than trusting the signature.

guards.what: N2 (DORMANT): `if (target == base.Owner.Creature) return amount;` (PaperPhrog.cs:18-21) -- no bonus when the phrog's own owner is the Vulnerable creature; the sim checks only the dealer
guards.issue: MECHANISM: paper_phrog.py:22 is `if dealer is self.player`, with no target check. Combined with the caller's requirement that the dealer be the phrog's owner (VulnerablePower.cs:40) and the power's requirement that the target be the Vulnerable holder (:29-32, mirrored at powers.py:407-408), the guard can only matter when the PLAYER is simultaneously the dealer, the Vulnerable creature, and dealing a POWERED attack -- i.e. a powered self-attack. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, executed -- `py tools/audit/relic_probes_b11.py phrog-selfhit`): the probe enumerates all 17 ported sites that deal damage TO the player and classifies each by props and dealer; the count that are both POWERED and player-dealt is ZERO. Every card that hurts its own player uses CARD_HP_LOSS or an unpowered variant (bad_luck, beckon, blood_wall, bloodletting, brand, burn, decay, hemokinesis, infection, offering, regret, toxic, wither), and the one powered site aimed at the player is a MONSTER attack (monsters/base.py:115, `dealer=self`). Porting any card or power that deals POWERED, Move-flagged damage from the player to the player makes it live -- and it would then be live in the SILENT direction: the sim would over-multiply the player's self-damage by 1.75 instead of 1.5. Recorded as a gap, not a waiver: 'no ported card does this' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1).

guards.what: N3: the sim's modify_vulnerable_multiplier hook takes only (dealer, mult), dropping C#'s target, props and cardSource parameters
guards.rationale: The dropped parameters are each accounted for above: target by N2 (a real, dormant divergence), props by N1 (structurally enforced upstream), and cardSource by nothing at all -- neither PaperPhrog nor CrueltyPower nor DebilitatePower reads it (`grep -n cardSource` over the three bodies shows it unused in every one), so it is a signature-only parameter. Recorded so the narrowed signature is on the record as examined rather than assumed harmless.

guards.what: N4 (PROMPT.md bug class 16): no RelicModel.IsAllowed override; no Rng draw; no state
guards.rationale: Executed grep over the batch's fifteen C# relic files finds no IsAllowed override, so sweep B's cluster excludes this unit. The relic is stateless, so bug class 13 has nothing to bite on -- consistent with its absence from sweep-reset's candidate list. Obtainability confirmed by execution (`py tools/audit/relic_probes_b11.py pool`): Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag; the C# pool entry is IroncladRelicPool.cs:25.
